description.content: This component efficiently displays arbitrarily positioned cells using windowing techniques. Cell position is determined by an injected cellPositioner property. Windowing is vertical; this component does not support horizontal scrolling.

Rendering occurs in two phases:

  1. First pass uses estimated cell sizes (provided by the cache) to determine how many cells to measure in a batch. Batch size is chosen using a fast, naive layout algorithm that stacks images in order until the viewport has been filled. After measurement is complete (once the render has been committed) this component evaluates positioned cells in order to determine if another measurement pass is required (eg if actual cell sizes were less than estimated sizes). All measurements are permanently cached (keyed by keyMapper) for performance purposes.
  2. Second pass uses the external cellPositioner to layout cells. At this time the positioner has access to cached size measurements for all cells. The positions it returns are cached by Masonry for fast access later. Phase one is repeated if the user scrolls beyond the current layout's bounds. If the layout is invalidated due to eg a resize, cached positions can be cleared using recomputeCellPositions().
Animation constraints: Simple animations are supported (eg translate/slide into place on initial reveal). More complex animations are not (eg flying from one position to another on resize).

Layout constraints: This component supports multi-column layout. The height of each item may vary. The width of each item must not exceed the width of the column it is "in". The left position of all items within a column must align. (Items may not span multiple columns.)
Optional ARIA label to attach to root Masonry element.
Total number of items.
Caches item measurements (typically an instance of CellMeasurerCache). Default sizes help Masonry decide how many images to batch-measure.
Positions a cell given an index: (index: number) => ({ left: number, top: number }). See createMasonryCellPositioner for a built-in positioner.

Responsible for rendering a cell given an index: ({ index: number, isScrolling: boolean, key: Key, parent: MasonryImperativeAPI, style: CSSProperties }) => ReactNode. The style param must be passed through to the rendered cell element. The cell should typically be wrapped in a CellMeasurer.
Optional custom CSS class name to attach to root Masonry element.

description.content: Height of the component; this value determines the number of visible items. Required, unless a scrollElement is specified.
With a scrollElement, the height of the scroll element's viewport is used instead; this prop is then only used until the scroll element has been measured (e.g. during server rendering).

description.content: Maps an index to a unique id to store cached measurement and position info for a cell. This prevents eg cached measurements from being invalidated when a collection is re-ordered. Defaults to the identity function (index => index).

Callback invoked with information about the cells that were most recently rendered. This callback is only invoked when visible cells have changed: ({ startIndex: number, stopIndex: number }): void. Does nothing by default.

description.content: Element that scrolls the Masonry (instead of the Masonry scrolling itself): "window", or a scrollable DOM element (e.g. a container that the Masonry is rendered within, along with other content).

The Masonry then renders at its full height, and renders only the cells visible within the scroll element's viewport. Its position within the scroll element is measured when the scroll element scrolls or is resized, and when the Masonry re-renders (e.g. call forceUpdate() if content above the Masonry changes size without the Masonry re-rendering). Pass null while the scroll element isn't available yet (e.g. before a ref to it has been attached); the Masonry then renders the cells at its top.
